name: analytics
title: Analytics
purpose: Observe interactions across installed Balsa components and route normalized or custom events to application-selected analytics providers.
useFor: One-place interaction analytics for Balsa components
avoidFor: Loading vendor scripts or deciding consent on behalf of the application
Collecting field values, visible text, destinations, or personal data automatically
Treating every interaction as a marketing conversion

composition.automaticEvent: Interactive descendants of data-balsa roots emit balsa_interaction with balsa_component, balsa_component_path, and balsa_action.
composition.customEvent: Button analyticsEvent and the data-balsa-track hook emit a second named event without suppressing the automatic event.
composition.privacyBoundary: Automatic collection never reads visible text, form values, URLs, or identifiers; context and transforms are explicit application code.
composition.providerBoundary: Adapters call already-configured browser tags and never inject tracking scripts. LinkedIn sends only explicitly mapped conversion events.

accessibility: The provider renders no element and does not alter component semantics, focus, keyboard handling, or default browser behavior.
Tracking runs after normal bubbling and never prevents or synthesizes an interaction.
The application remains responsible for consent, disclosure, retention, and provider configuration.
Disabled and loading controls retain their native Balsa behavior and do not create successful user interactions.
commonMistakes: Loading GA4, Meta Pixel, or the LinkedIn Insight Tag from the adapter instead of using the provider's official installation and consent flow.
Passing form values, email addresses, full URLs, or other sensitive data through context or a transform.
Mapping the automatic balsa_interaction event to a LinkedIn conversion instead of mapping a deliberate business event such as cta or lead.
Mounting more than one document-scoped provider and duplicating events.

examples.title: GA4 provider configuration
examples.description: Forward structural and custom Balsa events to an existing Google tag after analytics consent is granted.
examples.source:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
import BalsaAnalyticsProvider from "@/components/ui/BalsaAnalyticsProvider.vue";
import Button from "@/components/ui/Button.vue";
import { createGoogleAnalyticsAdapter } from "@/components/ui/analytics";

const analyticsConsent = ref(false);
const adapters = [
  createGoogleAnalyticsAdapter({ sendTo: "G-XXXXXXXXXX" }),
];
</script>

<template>
  <BalsaAnalyticsProvider
    :adapters="adapters"
    :enabled="analyticsConsent"
  >
    <Button analytics-event="cta">
      Start free trial
    </Button>
  </BalsaAnalyticsProvider>
</template>

examples.title: Application-owned adapter
examples.description: Send the normalized event contract to a reviewed first-party destination without adding a visual playground.
examples.source:
<script setup lang="ts">
import BalsaAnalyticsProvider from "@/components/ui/BalsaAnalyticsProvider.vue";
import Button from "@/components/ui/Button.vue";
import { createAnalyticsAdapter } from "@/components/ui/analytics";

const firstParty = createAnalyticsAdapter("first-party", (event) => {
  navigator.sendBeacon("/analytics", JSON.stringify(event));
});
</script>

<template>
  <BalsaAnalyticsProvider :adapters="[firstParty]">
    <Button analytics-event="lead">
      Request a demo
    </Button>
  </BalsaAnalyticsProvider>
</template>
